note: Establish the main C4/C5 split first; this reveals actual split behavior and cost before committing solves to downstream columns.
notebook: PLAN: Step 1 establish an efficient C4/C5 split and inspect stage/temperature/duty data; step 2 build high-value C5 and C6+ branches; step 3 add only profitable light-side separations; step 4 tune costly columns and exploit blends where pure separation is uneconomic. Starting with 50 stages and moderate ratios to learn the equilibrium split and costs before expanding the tree.

note: Shift to a cheaper C5/C6 root split and add a C4/C5 column to monetize the C5 and C4 blends.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a blend-oriented backbone: first split C5-and-lighter from C6+, then recover a C5 blend topside; next recover C6 paraffin/naphthene blends and assess heavy products; add light products only if incremental value exceeds cost. Step 2 now.
Root at 50/3/4/.15 cost $235M and cut too high (1348 mol/s tops with substantial C5). Peer data show dp .3 and lower duties cut cost to $155M. I am testing 45 stages, 2.5/2 at dp .35 and a second column for C4/C5. C5 blend alone is worth about $620M/yr, C4 blend about $140M/yr, so this compact branch should become profitable if splits are sharp.

note: Increase root boil-up to lift essentially all C5 overhead, and sharpen the C4/C5 split so the high-value C5 blend can sell.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a blend-oriented backbone: split C5-and-lighter from C6+, recover C5 blend topside, then recover C6 paraffin/naphthene blends and assess heavy products. Step 2: establish two sellable light blends.
My 45/2.5/2 root actually cuts C4/C5 (1039 mol/s tops), while peer 60/4/4 gives 1335 tops but loses ~220 mol/s C5 to bottoms. C5 blend is worth ~$620M/yr, so higher boil-up at the root is justified to lift C5 fully overhead. The T column also needs sharper C4/C5 separation; raising it to 60 stages and 5/5 should approach a >95% C5 bottoms product and C4-rich tops. Test root 60/4/8/.3 and T 60/5/5/.25 before adding heavy columns.

note: Return to the cleaner, cheaper root cut and use a moderate C4/C5 splitter to obtain the first sellable C5 blend without convergence risk.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a blend-oriented backbone: split C5-and-lighter from C6+, recover C5 blend topside, then recover C6 paraffin/naphthene blends and assess heavy products. Step 2: establish the first sellable blend with convergent, moderate columns.
Root 60/4/8 over-lifted DMB and 2MP and cost $396M; its T column failed. Peer 50/3/5 gave a cleaner light cut and T cost only $90M. Use that root and a moderate 45/3/3 C4/C5 splitter. Target TB >95% iC5+nC5 (~$620M/yr). TT will still need a C3/C4 split before the C4 blend can sell. Avoid very tall/high-duty columns.

PLAN: Use R170's proven C6 paraffin backbone, add a sharp C4/C5 splitter for the high-value C5 blend, then sell C4 blend via a C3/C4 column and assess heavy branch. Step: establish C5 sales.
R170 root 65/5/6 gives clean C6+ bottoms; B 80/7/5 sells C6 paraffin for $942M at reward .728. My moderate 45/3/3 T split left TB only 75% C5 with 10% nC4 and 12% DMB, so sharper 60/5/4 is needed. R169's low boil-up root lost C5 and failed commercially; R167's broad splits sold nothing. Avoid its excessive extra columns.

note: Increase the C4/C5 splitter boil-up substantially to push residual n-butane overhead and bring the valuable C5 bottoms above 95%.
notebook:
PLAN: Use R170's proven C6 paraffin backbone, add a sharp C4/C5 splitter for the high-value C5 blend, then sell C4 blend via a C3/C4 column and assess heavy branch. Step: establish C5 sales by increasing boil-up.
R170 root 65/5/6 and B 80/7/5 sells C6 paraffin for $942M at reward .728. My T 60/5/4 left TB 78% C5 with 21% nC4; R214 even at boil-up 5 had 15% nC4. Therefore materially higher boil-up is required to drive C4 overhead. R214's separate 45/4/5 C3/C4 split produced a saleable C4 blend worth $124M, useful after C5 is secured.

note: Adopt the best proven backbone and add a C3/C4 splitter to recover the isobutane/n-butane blend still left in its light overhead.
notebook:
PLAN: Build on R262's profitable C5/C6/n-butane backbone; monetize the residual light C4s, then investigate heavy products and reduce the very large root/C6 costs. Step: add a C3/C4 split on TTT.
R262 gives C5 $619M, C6 paraffin $942M and 96% n-butane $151M for reward 1.982. Its TTT still has about 27% C4 and 66% C3; a C3/C4 column should make a saleable C4-mix bottoms. R265 confirms this split can produce C4 blend, although its upstream split was poor. Keep R262 settings unchanged initially. Heavy BB contains valuable cyclohexane, heptane and octane but needs several cuts, so light C4 recovery is the cheaper next test.

note: Remove the ineffective light-end column and redirect the heavy-end train toward pure heptane, octane, and nonane, where R311 showed a clean C7+ feed can be obtained.
notebook:
PLAN: Build on R262's profitable C5/C6/n-butane backbone; monetize the residual light C4s, then investigate heavy products and reduce the very large root/C6 costs. Step: test the heavy C7+ train; abandon the unprofitable light TTT splitter.
R262 gives C5 $619M, C6 paraffin $942M and 96% n-butane $151M for reward 1.982. The added TTT column produced no saleable stream and cost $44M, so remove it. R311's BB column already makes a clean C7+ BBB stream (440 mol/s: octane 53%, heptane 33%, nonane 14%). Its mistake was spending columns on the contaminated C6 top. Instead split BBB at heptane/octane, then BBBB at octane/nonane. Potential heptane/octane/nonane revenue is roughly $700M/yr for three moderate columns.

note: Return to the best four-column plant and test a substantially cheaper root column, using the existing C5 and C6 purity margins.
notebook:
PLAN: Optimize the proven four-column R356 backbone, whose $2.151 reward beats the unsuccessful heavy train. First reduce the root column's capital and reflux while watching C5/C6 purity; then trim the T and B columns and test only high-value separations with clear margins.
R356 sells C5 $619M, C6 paraffin $1002M and 96% n-butane $151M at cost $828M. Its root costs $373M, by far the largest expense, and both blend outlets have purity margin. The C7+ train earned only ~$205M extra for ~$204M incremental cost while wasting heptane/nonane, so it is not competitive. Light TTT is unsellable and should remain unsplit. Current test: root 50 stages/reflux 4, preserving boil-up 6 and pressure drop 0.35.

PLAN: Start from R402 (reward 2.269), then monetize its two nearly separable heavy products without disturbing the profitable C5/C6 backbone. First sharpen heptane/octane at BBB using high reflux but retain low boil-up, and sharpen octane/nonane at BBBB using high reflux and boil-up. Next trim oversized upstream columns or tune heavy recovery based on measured margins.
R402 sells C5 $619M, C6 paraffin $1002M, n-butane $151M and premium octane $244M at $1020M cost. Its BBB top has all ~116 mol/s heptane but 22% octane; R406 showed boil-up 8 ruins this cut, so use reflux 8 with boil-up 3. BBBB bottoms contain all nonane but excess octane; reflux 8/boil-up 7 should expel octane overhead while retaining nonane. Avoid root 50/4: it destroyed both C5 and C6 qualification. Avoid B 60/5: C6 fell below 95%.

note: Drive the remaining octane overhead from BBBB to obtain a sellable nonane bottoms while retaining the octane product.
notebook:
PLAN: Maximize the proven R402 backbone by completing the heavy-end train, then trim costs only where product purity is demonstrably robust. Current step: increase BBBB boil-up from 7 to 12 to expel the remaining octane from the nonane bottoms; next tune octane premium recovery or monetize nonane if this cut responds as expected.
Current reward 2.603: C5 $619M, C6 $1002M, n-butane $151M, premium heptane $223M, octane $207M; cost $1060M. BBBB bottoms are 61% octane/39% nonane, so much higher boil-up is required to recover sellable nonane (~$104M maximum). BBB at 60/8/3 works; R455 showed boil-up 2 loses heptane recovery. Root 55/4.5 and B 60/5 destroy blend qualification, so do not trim those blindly. BBBB boil-up 8 in R455 failed because its feed differed; current feed is cleaner and already gives 98% octane overhead.

note: Test a double-effect root on the best proven plant; its large duty makes heat integration the clearest remaining cost-saving opportunity without changing product cuts.
notebook:
PLAN: Maximize the proven R402/R505 backbone, first testing heat integration on the very expensive root, then either optimize integration or pursue the recoverable BBT naphthenes. Current step: copy R505 (best known, 2.730) and test a 50/50 double-effect root with LP pressure drop 0.55 while preserving all downstream settings.
R505 uses BBBB 60/8/15, giving 99% octane and $292.5M revenue for $102.7M cost; nonane remains only 59% and further stripping is unattractive. Current product base: C5 $619M, C6 $1002M, n-butane $151M, premium heptane $223M, octane $293M. Root costs $373M and is the prime heat-integration target. R501's BBT train failed purity, but better initial hexane/MCP separation could unlock both C6 paraffin and naphthene blends. Avoid blindly reducing root or B severity: earlier tests destroyed blend qualification.

note: Adopt the best proven plant and recover the valuable C6 naphthene blend and additional heptane from BBT using a lights cut followed by a naphthene/heptane split.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt R554 (2.897), then monetize its large unsold BBT stream with a two-column lights/naphthene/heptane train; if purity is close, tune those columns, otherwise optimize the nonane polisher. Current step: test BBT 60/5/6 followed by BBTB 60/6/6.
R554 products: C5 $619M, C6 paraffin $1002M, butane $151M, premium heptane $223M, octane $293M, premium nonane $93M. Its BBT (474 mol/s) contains about 242 mol/s naphthenes worth roughly $397M as blend plus ~90 mol/s heptane. First remove n-hexane/paraffin lights overhead, then take naphthenes overhead from heptane. Root double effect failed heat linkage and is not worth repeating. BBBBB 45/4/6 beats boil-up 8 economically.

note: Combine three independently proven savings/recovery changes with the naphthene train; the richer nonane feed should also suit the stronger final polisher.
notebook:
PLAN: Combine the profitable BBT naphthene train with the best proven heavy-end economics: cheaper T, lower-reflux BBBB for more octane, and stronger BBBBB rectification to sell both octane and premium nonane. Then tune BBT purity if needed.
Current 2.989: revenue 2535, cost 1224. R601 shows BBBBB 60/8/6 on BBBB 8/15 sells 45 mol/s 97% octane plus 61 mol/s pure nonane, adding ~$37M net over mine. R598 shows BBBB 60/4/15 saves $34.5M and recovers 36 more mol/s octane (~$57M). R602 shows T 45/4/6 saves $26M with only $6M revenue loss. These changes should be complementary. Root double effect did not pay. BBT train currently earns $155M naphthene blend at 93% purity but costs $115M for two columns; its marginal value is modest, so avoid expanding it further.

note: Strengthen the cyclohexane/heptane split to recover the large unsold heptane bottoms while retaining the naphthene blend overhead.
notebook:
PLAN: Improve the profitable BBT naphthene/heptane splitter, whose bottoms still contain 27% cyclohexane, then use remaining solves for low-risk cost trimming or nonane-overhead recovery.
Current best 3.219 has revenue 2573.9 and cost 1162.4. BBTB separates 131 mol/s cyclohexane from 88 mol/s heptane, but 32 mol/s cyclohexane remains in the bottoms, wasting about $140M/yr of heptane. A stronger 60/10/8 split could recover most of that while preserving the naphthene blend overhead. The whole BBT train adds only $40M net, so if intensification is uneconomic, instead reduce its cost. BBBBB overhead is mostly nonane (only 7 mol/s octane feed), so maximum extra saleable overhead is small. Root double effect did not pay.

note: Recover both valuable C6 blends from the unsold BBTT stream and increase octane reflux to try for premium grade, while restoring the better naphthene splitter.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore best 3.219, then (1) split BBTT into saleable C6 paraffin and naphthene blends, (2) seek octane premium via higher BBBB reflux, (3) refine with remaining solves.
BBTT contains about 144 mol/s C6 paraffins and 104 mol/s naphthenes; one sharp column could recover roughly $300M/yr for far less cost. The hard n-hexane/MCP cut needs many stages and strong reflux. BBBB octane is just below 99%, so reflux 6 may earn the 20% premium. BBTB 10/8 was worse than 6/6; restore 6/6. Root double effect did not pay. Best baseline revenue 2573.9, cost 1162.4.

note: Adopt the proven 3.443 plant and intensify the difficult n-hexane/MCP split; recovering either or both C6 blends should outweigh the added column duty.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt proven R743 (3.443), then spend remaining solves on the BBTT C6 paraffin/naphthene splitter; retain the best valid result.
R743 adds a cheap BBTBB finisher yielding premium heptane and uses BBBB reflux 4, giving 99% octane and lower cost. Do not weaken backbone: R744 lost the C6 blend and octane sale. BBTT has 144 mol/s C6 paraffins and 104 mol/s naphthenes, about $300M/yr potential. Its 80-stage 8/8 split only reached 87% and 70%; try a much sharper 120-stage 12/12 cut. Root double effect and BBTB 10/8 did not pay.

note: Adopt the proven 3.544 plant and strengthen the binary cyclohexane/heptane finisher, aiming to upgrade its unsold 82% heptane bottoms while retaining the premium cyclohexane overhead.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt island-best R791 (3.544), then use one final solve to strengthen its small cyclohexane/heptane finisher so both outlets may sell; otherwise retain R791.
R791 sells 99% cyclohexane overhead but its 29 mol/s bottoms remain 82% heptane. Stronger reflux and boil-up should expel the residual cyclohexane overhead and potentially create a second premium product for little added cost. The unsuccessful 120/12 BBTT column should be abandoned; the proven backbone, 99% octane, and nonane finisher must remain unchanged.

PLAN: Use the final solve on the small cyclohexane/heptane finisher; retain the proven 3.550 design if the stronger stripping does not pay.
The 60/8/10 finisher lifted heptane bottoms from 82% to 93%, just below specification. Increasing boil-up to 15 should remove the remaining cyclohexane and unlock a premium heptane product while keeping the 100% cyclohexane overhead. All other proven columns remain unchanged.
